error_model.value: average polling miss per party's vote share in a competitive state 'a hair over 2 points', ~3.8 pts on margin
errors drawn from Student's t with 5 degrees of freedom

pairwise state correlations predicted by regression on historical vote similarity (since 1948), demographic similarity (ACS race, Hispanic, age, income, white non-college; PRRI evangelical; density) and 538 political regions; bias correlated across states; no separate national SD given
SD ~6 pts; would miss average state margin by ~6.5 pts
polling_bias_scale = 0.013 on vote-share (probability) scale; state bias vector ~ MVN scaled so the state-weighted national bias has that SD
C = cor of state demographic/political variables (2016 vote, ACS, urbanicity, white evangelical %), negatives set to 0; final = 0.75*C + 0.25*(all-ones) 'to correspond to national-level error'
fundamentals RMSE(days) = 0.03 + 10^-6.6*days^2; random walk 0.05/sqrt(300) per day; logit-scale priors: pollster 0.06, mode 0.04, population(LV/RV/adult) 0.04, measurement noise 0.04, e_bias 0.02
nearly all 2024 polls missed in same direction so averaging offered little help; Trump sweeping all 7 swing states was the model's single most likely outcome, Harris sweep next
bias 'historically unpredictable cycle-to-cycle'; avg since 1998 D+1.1

lagged bias got direction right 10 of 14 cycles; magnitude missed by 2.5 pts on avg; slope 0.57 (SE 0.38); bias-adjustment would have worsened 10 of 14 Election Day forecasts; polls miss 'by similar amounts' across races each cycle

overstated Biden margin in nearly every state; state signed error regression: Trump-2016 share 0.25*, %Black -0.33*, log density 1.27*, adj R2 0.48; Senate polls overstated D more than presidential polls in same state
